note_tweet.text:
Your AI employee just got a second desk.

OpenAI's dots can now connect to multiple local computers. One dot, several machines — you pick which one runs each task. Build and test your app on the spare box while you keep coding on your laptop.

Until yesterday, a dot got one machine. That was the bottleneck: the always-on agent in the cloud had exactly one foothold on your desk, and every local job queued through it.

And it's still Pro and up. Free and Plus don't get dots at all.

Here's the catch. Each thread still runs on one computer at a time, and there are no per-machine permissions. One "Allow access" hands the dot that machine's files, code, and apps — all of it, not the folder you meant.

So the upgrade is real, and so is the trade. The dot that builds on your spare machine is the same dot that can read everything on it.

The multi-computer update isn't about more computers. It's about how much of your desk you're willing to hand over.
